description: issue #874: `params.callable` is the name as its DEFINITION declares it — for a learner's own procedure, the spelling their `define` wrote, reported identically from every call site. Here `define MyProc` is called as `(MYPROC 1 2)` and the finding still says `MyProc`. Identifiers are case-insensitive, so `MyProc`/`myproc`/`MYPROC` name one procedure and therefore one condition, which `spec/error-model.md:254-259` requires to carry one set of structured params; before this the checker echoed the CALL SITE, so one defect produced three different identities depending on how it happened to be typed. THIS FIXTURE EXISTS BECAUSE EVERY OTHER `callable` FIXTURE IS BLIND TO THE RULE: all of them (including arity-not-enough-procedure and struct-constructor-arity-too-few) use all-lowercase names, where the declared spelling, the call site, and the lowercased form coincide — so they pass under any of the three candidate rules and cannot pin this one. Mixed case is the whole point of the fixture.
